high.title: Peso Slides Back to P61 Level on Uncertainty Over US-Iran Talks
high.summary: The Philippine peso depreciated by 23.5 centavos to close at P61.165/USD on Tuesday, reversing Monday's strength (close: P60.93), driven by mixed signals surrounding US-Iran peace negotiations. The uncertainty rekindled risk-off sentiment, pressuring the peso alongside renewed weakness in the Japanese yen — notably just one day after a coordinated yen intervention effort by Japanese authorities had temporarily stabilized the currency. The peso had briefly traded stronger intraday before selling pressure dominated. For FX traders, this episode underscores how geopolitical risk premiums — particularly Middle East developments — remain a key driver of PHP volatility, with spillover effects from JPY dynamics also influencing regional EM currency sentiment. The P61 level is a psychologically and technically significant threshold; a sustained breach could attract further speculative selling. Traders should closely monitor progress (or breakdown) in US-Iran talks, global crude oil price movements, and any BSP verbal or market intervention signals as key near-term catalysts.

high.title: BTr Fully Awards Bonds as Rates Decline on Easing Middle East Tensions
high.summary: The Bureau of the Treasury (BTr) successfully raised the full planned P30 billion from a reissued 20-year Treasury bond auction, drawing P93.8 billion in total tenders — a bid-to-cover ratio of over 3x — signaling robust domestic investor demand. Declining rates were attributed to improving sentiment linked to easing Middle East tensions, which weighed on global crude oil prices and tempered inflation expectations. For Philippine government bond investors, this auction result is materially bullish: the oversubscription at the long end of the curve suggests that institutional investors are comfortable extending duration, implying expectations of a benign inflation and rate outlook. The strong demand may also reflect continued domestic liquidity seeking fixed-income alternatives. Bond traders should note that geopolitical de-escalation and lower oil prices could support further yield compression across the PHP sovereign curve, while any reversal in ME tensions — as hinted by the same-day peso weakness article — represents a key upside risk to yields. Watch for the BTr's next auction calendar and BSP's rate guidance.

high.title: Hot Money Inflows Hit $170M in June
high.summary: Net foreign portfolio investment (FPI) inflows into the Philippines reached $170.12 million in June, marking the second consecutive month of net inflows according to BSP data. While the June figure is lower than May's $232.46 million, the sustained positive trend signals improving foreign investor confidence in Philippine financial assets despite ongoing global market volatility. For PHP and PSEi traders, consecutive months of hot money inflows provide a modest but meaningful support factor for the peso and equity markets, as these flows require USD-to-PHP conversion and domestic asset purchases. However, the declining momentum from May to June warrants monitoring — any shift to net outflows could amplify peso depreciation pressure, particularly given the currency's current vulnerability around the P61 level. Key variables to watch include global risk appetite, US Federal Reserve rate trajectory, and Philippine-specific macro catalysts such as inflation prints and BSP policy decisions, all of which influence the stickiness of these portfolio flows.

high.title: BofA Sees BSP Ending Its Tightening Cycle in August
high.summary:
Bank of America Global Research expects the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) to deliver a final 25 basis point rate hike at its August 27 meeting — contingent on July inflation printing below 7% year-on-year — which would bring the benchmark policy rate to 5.00%. BofA characterizes this as the likely terminal rate, marking the end of the current tightening cycle. This is a critical signal for PHP and Philippine government bond traders. A confirmed cycle peak at 5.00% would remove further rate-hike risk premium from the front end of the yield curve, potentially triggering a bond rally as investors price in a plateau or eventual easing. For FX, the PHP outlook will hinge on whether the BSP's terminal rate is sufficient to maintain the interest rate differential versus the USD and contain inflation expectations. **Key watch:** July CPI release (expected shortly) — a print above 7% could delay or complicate the BSP's pivot narrative, while a sub-7% figure validates the BofA call and may prompt positioning shifts in both bonds and PHP.

---

high.title: TDF Yield Goes Up on Rate Hike Bets as Inflation Stays Elevated
high.summary: The BSP's term deposit facility (TDF) auction saw weaker-than-expected demand, with bids totaling only P129.622 billion against P150 billion in seven-day papers on offer — resulting in a bid-to-cover ratio of just 0.80x, undersubscribed relative to both the offering size and the prior week's P137.524 billion in tenders. Critically, yields moved higher as investors price in further monetary policy tightening, reflecting persistent inflation concerns following July's elevated CPI print. This is a high-signal data point for PHP bond and rates traders: undersubscription in TDF auctions combined with rising short-end yields suggests the market is positioning for an additional BSP rate hike, steepening the near-term rates outlook. For government bond investors, this dynamic may push yields higher across the short-to-medium curve. PHP could see two-way volatility — rate hike expectations are broadly supportive of the peso via carry, but elevated inflation erodes real returns. **Watch:** BSP's next policy meeting guidance and upcoming August CPI data for confirmation of the tightening bias.

high.title: Peso Surges as Iran Deal Hopes Hit Dollar
high.summary: The Philippine peso posted a sharp 41.4-centavo appreciation on Wednesday, closing at P60.751 per dollar from P61.165 the prior session — its strongest close in nearly seven weeks (since June 18's P60.567). The primary driver was broad USD weakness triggered by optimism surrounding progress in US-Iran peace negotiations, which reduced geopolitical risk premiums and softened safe-haven dollar demand globally. The session opened at P60.9, indicating strong intraday momentum in favor of the peso. For FX traders, this move signals that external geopolitical developments — rather than domestic fundamentals — are currently the dominant near-term driver of USD/PHP. The pair's breach below P61.00 is technically significant and may invite further tests toward the P60.50 support zone. **Key risk:** If Iran talks stall or reverse, dollar demand could snap back quickly. Domestic inflation and rate hike expectations provide a supportive underpinning for PHP, but geopolitical headline risk remains the swing factor in the near term.

high.title: Bessent's Call to Upsize US Federal Reserve's Foreign Lending Facility May Not Be Risk-Free
high.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has called for the Federal Reserve to expand the Foreign and International Monetary Authorities (FIMA) repo facility — a dollar liquidity tool that allows foreign central banks to swap US Treasuries for USD cash. While the immediate context focuses on Japan's yen defense, the implications extend to all EM central banks, including the BSP, which could potentially access greater dollar liquidity in stress scenarios. However, analysts warn that expanding the facility could embolden markets to test central bank resolve, creating moral hazard. For PHP traders and BSP watchers, this is a medium-term structural development: broader FIMA access could reduce the cost of FX intervention for EM central banks, potentially giving the BSP more firepower to defend the peso during bouts of USD strength. **Watch:** Whether the Fed formally agrees to expand the cap, and how BSP's reserve management strategy might adapt if access to dollar liquidity channels is widened.

high.title: July Inflation Cools to 4-Month Low
high.summary:
Philippine headline inflation decelerated to 6.2% year-on-year in July 2026, down from 6.4% in June, marking the slowest pace in four months (the last comparable reading was 4.1% in March). The PSA attributed the moderation primarily to easing transport costs and a steadying in food inflation. While the directional trend is encouraging, the absolute level at 6.2% remains materially above the BSP's target band, leaving the central bank in a challenging policy position. For PHP and bond traders, this print is net positive on the margin — it reduces pressure on the BSP to deliver additional aggressive rate hikes and may open the door to a more dovish forward guidance tone. Government bond yields could rally modestly at the short end on reduced rate-hike premium. However, with inflation still running at elevated levels relative to the BSP's target and a year-ago base of just 0.9% (suggesting base effects will become less favorable), the disinflation path remains fragile. Watch for the BSP's next policy meeting commentary and any guidance on whether this print shifts the rate trajectory. GDP data due this week adds another key variable for the policy outlook.

---

medium.title: BSP Partners with KasKasan Buddies for Financial Literacy
medium.summary:
The BSP's digital financial education platform PisoLit has entered into a partnership with KasKasan Buddies, one of the Philippines' largest online financial communities, to produce social media content and learning sessions aimed at improving financial literacy among Filipinos. While this is primarily a public engagement initiative rather than a market-moving development, it reflects the BSP's broader strategic push to deepen financial inclusion and retail participation in formal financial markets. Greater financial literacy could incrementally support domestic participation in government securities, mutual funds, and capital markets over the medium term — a modest structural positive for market depth and local bond demand.

---

medium.title: PSEi Falls to 6,200 Range as Traders Lock In Gains
medium.summary: The PSEi retreated 0.60% or 38.08 points to close at 6,296.64, with the broader All Shares Index also declining 0.43% to 3,415.35, as investors booked profits following a sharp rally in the prior session. Sentiment remained cautious amid ongoing uncertainty surrounding US-Iran peace negotiations, which weighed on risk appetite across the region. The pullback appears technical in nature rather than driven by domestic macro deterioration. For equity-focused fund managers, the 6,200–6,300 range represents near-term support to monitor; a sustained hold above this level would be constructive, while a break lower could signal broader risk-off pressure affecting PHP and local assets simultaneously.

medium.title: Philippine Exports Seen Resilient Despite 12.5% US Tariff
medium.summary: Analysts expect Philippine merchandise exports to remain broadly resilient under the US's 12.5% tariff regime, as key sectors — notably semiconductors and electronics — retain exemption status, shielding the country's primary export earners. However, labor-intensive sectors such as garments and leather goods face meaningful competitiveness risks, which could translate into job losses. From a macro and FX perspective, export resilience is crucial for sustaining the current account and supporting PHP. If electronics exemptions hold, the negative impact on the trade balance should remain manageable, limiting downside pressure on the peso. **Watch:** Any change in the exemption status of semiconductor exports would be a material negative for PHP and the current account outlook.

medium.title: PDIC Pushes Legislative Agenda to Boost Protection, Financial Stability
medium.summary:
The Philippine Deposit Insurance Corp. (PDIC) is seeking legislative reforms to expand its mandate, including extending deposit insurance coverage to non-bank financial institutions (NBFIs) and cooperatives, and raising coverage limits for higher-value accounts. While not a direct FX or rates market mover, this development is relevant to Philippine banking sector stability and systemic risk assessment. Broader deposit insurance coverage, if enacted, would reduce tail-risk concerns in the financial system and could modestly support investor confidence in Philippine financial assets. Fund managers with exposure to Philippine bank equities or bonds should monitor the legislative timeline, as expanded PDIC coverage may affect bank funding costs and liability structures over the medium term.

---

medium.title: Stocks Slip as Risk-Off Mood Persists Before GDP
medium.summary:
The PSEi declined 0.16% (−10.33 points) to close at 6,286.31 on Wednesday, with the broader All Shares index also slipping 0.07% to 3,412.82, reflecting persistent risk-off sentiment ahead of the Q2 GDP release. Notably, the market failed to sustain a rally despite the better-than-expected July CPI print and easing global oil prices, suggesting investor caution is driven by macro uncertainty rather than inflation concerns alone. The upcoming GDP data is the critical near-term catalyst — a strong print could restore risk appetite and support the PSEi, while a disappointing figure may reinforce the bearish tone. For equity-focused fund managers, the index's inability to respond positively to a favorable inflation surprise is a cautionary signal on near-term momentum.

---
